items.title: Basic Injection
items.summary:
See if you can leak the whole database using what you know about SQL Injections.
TL;DR Basic Injection is a fundamental web exploitation challenge demonstrating classic SQL Injection. The backend query incorporates user input directly via string concatenation without parameterization. Submitting a tautology payload (' OR 1=1 -- -) forces the SQL statement to evaluate to true for every record in the table, dumping the entire database contents and revealing the flag. Initial Analysis Opening the target application presents a simple query form that takes a user’s name:

items.title: Binwalk
items.summary:
Here is a file with another file hidden inside it. Can you extract it?
TL;DR Binwalk is an introductory digital forensics challenge that focuses on file carving and detecting embedded artifacts within image containers. Inspecting the file headers reveals an anomaly where a PNG file is masquerading under a .jpeg extension with extra data trailing the IEND chunk. Carving the hidden binary via foremost or binwalk extracts a secondary image displaying the flag. File Analysis We are given an image file named PurpleThing.jpeg .

items.summary:
The flag used to be there. But then I redacted it. Good Luck.

While the working tree file flag.txt only contains a decoy ___FL0X___ , inspecting the commit history using git log and diffing previous revisions with git show reveals the original plaintext flag before it was overwritten.
